text: who cuts hair, sharpens knives, pulls teeth, drains blood, and probably brews his own beer
in the same bucket he uses for amputations. He doesn't wear gloves. He doesn't wash his hands.
Soap exists. Technically. But it's expensive. And he's saving it for special occasions. Like never.
You walk in, clutching your stomach, and before you can even say what's wrong,
he already knows the diagnosis. Your humors are unbalanced. That was medieval science.
They believed your body was filled with four magical fluids.
Blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile. And when one of them got out of balance,
you got sick. Simple solution. Drain you like a water barrel. He ties a rag around your arm,
grabs a rusty blade that looks suspiciously like a butter knife, and opens a vein to let the bad
blood out. You came in dehydrated, and now you're leaving with half your blood volume gone,
and a 50% chance of passing out in the mud outside. He might even ask for a sample of your urine.
A common method back then. Not to test it. Just to stare at it,
and guess what's wrong by the color or the smell.
If bloodletting doesn't work, and it never does, there's always leeches. He keeps a jar of them,
squirming in what used to be someone's bathwater. He slaps a few on your skin,
and waits for them to suck until they fall off. Still not cured? Don't worry,
there's one more treatment. Prayer. Because of cutting, bleeding, and leeches don't work,
clearly you've just angered God. And if you don't start feeling better soon,
someone's going to start whispering that maybe, just maybe, you've been cursed by a witch.
